title: Quantum Query Lower Bounds for Triangle-Listing and Spanners
authors: Yu Chen, Ananta Mukherjee, Mingyang Yang
abstract: This paper gives quantum query lower bounds for two relational graph problems, triangle listing and explicit multiplicative spanner construction, in the general graph query model, where quantum adjacency, degree and neighborhood queries are all available in arbitrary superposition. Both results are obtained by reductions via intermediate multi-block search problems. We extend the quantum query recording framework by Zhandry (CRYPTO 2019) and Hamoudi and Magniez (ToCT 2023) to handle a recording architecture for bidirectional oracles and give a generic blockwise soundness framework, which for arbitrary families of local accepting projectors, gives an exact operator-norm characterization of their maximum overlap with the subspace of bounded weight records. Using the intermediate search problems, we exhibit a family of $n$-vertex graphs with $Θ(n)$ triangles on which listing any constant fraction of the triangles requires $Ω(n^{3/2-o(1)})$ quantum queries. This is the first nontrivial quantum lower bound for triangle listing, a question raised by Jiang and Peng (ICML 2026). Further, we show that, for every fixed $k\ge 7$, constructing a multiplicative $k$-spanner requires $Ω(n^{1+\frac{1}{2μ_k}})$ quantum queries, where $μ_k=k/3+O(1)$. For $k\in\{7,8\}$ the bound is $Ω(n^{5/4})$, which matches what would be implied by an unproven instance of the Erdős girth conjecture, and for large $k$ the exponent $1+\frac{3}{2k}$ exceeds the $1+\frac{4}{3k}$ implied by the provable high girth dense graphs due to Lazebnik, Ustimenko and Woldar, 1995.
summary: This paper determines quantum query lower bounds for graph problems like triangle listing and spanner construction within the general graph query model. It extends the quantum query recording framework to prove these bounds by reducing the graph problems to intermediate search tasks. The results establish significant theoretical limits on the efficiency of quantum algorithms for analyzing graph structure.
main_problem: The paper establishes quantum query lower bounds for two specific relational graph problems: listing all triangles in a graph and constructing a multiplicative spanner.
main_result: It achieves a first non-trivial quantum lower bound for triangle listing ($\Omega(n^{3/2-o(1)})$) and provides a bound for $k$-spanner construction ($\Omega(n^{1 + 1/2\mu_k})$).
method: The analysis extends the quantum query recording framework to handle bidirectional oracles, deriving bounds by reducing the graph problems to intermediate multi-block search problems (BHVF and RMIF).
model_or_system: The work operates in the general graph query model, utilizing quantum query complexity theory. The core technical tool is the 'recording method,' which tracks information across multiple query steps in a shared quantum record.
key_observables: Quantum query complexity, recording progress ($\Delta_{t,k}$), and the success probability of finding hidden values.
important_parameters: Graph size ($n$), number of blocks ($B$), size of the hidden space ($N$), and the target spanner parameter ($k$).
main_assumptions: The results are derived under the general graph query model (mixed model). The $k$-spanner bounds are compared against conjectures related to the Erdős girth conjecture.
paper_structure: The paper first extends the quantum query recording framework for bidirectional oracles and establishes a generic blockwise soundness lemma. It then uses this framework to derive lower bounds for intermediate search problems (BHVF/RMIF), which are subsequently used to prove the final bounds for triangle listing and $k$-spanner construction.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of advanced quantum query complexity techniques, particularly the recording method, to fundamental graph problems provides deep insights into the inherent computational difficulty of graph structure discovery.
